abstract: T-cell receptor (TCR) antigen recognition depends on the three-dimensional geometry of the paired {beta} complementarity-determining regions (CDRs), which primary sequence does not fully capture. Most repertoire-clustering methods group receptors by CDR3 motifs, sequence distance or V-J gene usage, and may miss receptors that differ in sequence but adopt similar loop conformations. We present SPACE-TCR (Structural Profiling of Alpha-Beta Clonotypes by Epitope), which stratifies predicted paired {beta} backbone models by CDR length, aligns them on conserved framework anchors and clusters them by C RMSD across the CDRs. On an independently curated benchmark of 4,779 paired CD8 TCRs spanning 367 epitopes, 94.6% of SPACE-TCR clusters at the focal 0.75 [A] threshold had purity [≥] 0.9, close to ClusTCR (97.3%), while clustering more than twice as many unique CDR3{beta} (10.4% versus 4.7%); every method that clustered more did so at markedly lower purity. SPACE-TCR had the lowest polyspecificity (5.4%), and 22.7% of its high-purity clusters were sequence-diverse or sequence-unrelated, categories rarely recovered by the evaluated CDR3{beta}-similarity methods. With increasing unannotated repertoire background, it kept higher purity than the evaluated sequence-based methods across all available comparisons (30.4% at 89.2% noise, compared with 15.0% for TCRMatch). Paired structural clustering therefore complements sequence-based analysis, recovering convergent receptor families that sequence criteria miss.
